issues.quote: Uncle Aurèle held it up in front of everyone like a dead fish and said it was a wreck and he would not have it in his house.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives only F1's reading (twenty to nine at nine o'clock) and says nothing about the accuracy of Félix's watch.
issues.misreading: The 'wreck' remark, and the later claim that the uncle could 'put it right' and that the repeater was 'the only honest thing in the house, because it told you the time when you asked', imply Félix's silver watch keeps poor time. A solver could discount or adjust every watch reading (9pm, 10pm, 10:15, 10:21, 10:32) and reach different times for the events.

issues.quote: At a quarter past ten by my watch someone went quickly up the stairs past the library door. I didn't see who. The door was shut. Then at twenty-one minutes past ten by my watch someone came quickly down.
issues.fact: F4 says the ascent at 10:15 came before the thump, and gives the descent at 10:21 with no stated order relative to the thump at 10:18.
issues.misreading: The witness narrates the descent (10:21) before the thump (10:18), so a solver could take the thump as coming after the descent, or the 'Then' as putting the thump in sequence after both movements.

issues.quote: I was alone in a room directly under his bench, drinking his brandy
issues.fact: F3 says only that the thump was on the floor right above the library, in the atelier. It does not say where the uncle's bench is.
issues.misreading: The sentence places the uncle's bench in the room above the library, which a solver could use to locate the bench, or the uncle at it, relative to the library.
